_comment: The harness chokepoint. packages/manifest.json says WHAT to install and
scripts/hostenv.py says HOW to reach it; this file says WHO consumes it.
Adding support for a new agent runtime is an edit here and nowhere else.
No script may hardcode a skills directory or an MCP config path.
Fields:
label        human name, printed in audits
detect       paths whose existence proves the harness is installed. A
harness that is absent is skipped, not created — we do not
scatter ~/.cursor on a machine that has no Cursor.
skills_dirs  directories that get one symlink per skill. Empty means the
harness reads somebody else's directory; see `covered_by`.
covered_by   harness keys whose skills_dirs this runtime already reads.
Linking again would register every skill two or three times.
registry     skills.json files listing skill SOURCE directories. Merged,
never overwritten: agent-skill-forge writes the same files.
mcp.scope    'project' writes inside this repo, which is how a server
stays opt-in. 'user' is global and is therefore never
written automatically — install_mcp.py prints the command.
mcp.format   mcpServers | opencode | codex-toml — the three shapes the
ecosystem has converged on, and they are not compatible.
mcp.portable true only where ${HOME} expansion in the config is a
documented, verified feature. Everyone else gets a real
absolute path and a gitignored file that install_mcp.py
regenerates per machine — a harness that does not expand
the variable would treat '${HOME}' as a literal directory.
Paths verified 2026-09-27 against each vendor's current documentation.

mcp.note: Project scope shows servers as '⏸ Pending approval' until approved in a session.

codex.label: OpenAI Codex
_skills_note: Codex's documented user-level location is ~/.agents/skills, shared with
the Universal Agent Hub. ~/.codex/skills is kept because older builds
read it and an extra symlink costs nothing; ~/.codex itself holds

mcp.note: Codex has no project-scope MCP config, so writing this would enable the server everywhere.

agents-hub.label: Universal Agent Hub
_always_note: The one directory created whether or not anything is detected. It is
the vendor-neutral location Codex and opencode both document, so on a
freshly imaged box — where no harness config exists yet — the skills
are already waiting when the first agent CLI starts. Every other
harness has to be present before we write into its home.

opencode.label: opencode
_skills_note: ~/.agents/skills. We populate the last two, so linking into the first
as well would show every skill three times in its picker.

cursor.label: Cursor
_skills_note: Cursor has no skills directory of its own; it reads .claude/skills.
Its agent picks up this repo's skills when opened as a project.
